boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Maryland-Baltimore County
boards.description: Ten currently documented food and campus destinations with evening or overnight availability around UMBC.

cards.title: True Grit's Market
cards.subtitle: UMBC campus, Baltimore, MD
cards.notes: Check UMBC OpenNow before heading over; it lists True Grit's Outtakes as open from 6 a.m. to 3 a.m. for a late campus option.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus market with overnight-listed availability.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC OpenNow lists “True Grit's Outtakes” as open 6 a.m.–3 a.m.
cards.source_title: UMBC OpenNow
cards.access_notes: UMBC OpenNow currently lists the location as 6 a.m.–3 a.m.; verify the live listing before going.

cards.title: 2.Mato
cards.subtitle: The Commons, UMBC campus
cards.notes: Use the live UMBC OpenNow listing to confirm service before walking over; it currently shows 2.Mato open until 10 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A Commons food counter listed into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC OpenNow currently lists 2.Mato as open from noon to 10 p.m.
cards.source_title: UMBC OpenNow
cards.access_notes: The live UMBC listing currently shows noon–10 p.m.; campus dining schedules can change.

cards.title: Outtakes (Commons)
cards.subtitle: The Commons, UMBC campus
cards.notes: Check the live UMBC listing before leaving your residence; it currently lists Outtakes in The Commons through 10 p.m.
cards.short_summary: An evening-listed convenience-food stop in The Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC OpenNow currently lists Outtakes (Commons) as open from noon to 10 p.m.
cards.source_title: UMBC OpenNow
cards.access_notes: The live UMBC listing currently shows noon–10 p.m.; confirm status before visiting.

cards.title: The Commons
cards.subtitle: 1000 Hilltop Circle, UMBC campus
cards.notes: Plan a Friday or Saturday stop around the building schedule; The Commons publishes midnight closing on those two regular-semester nights.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s student-union building stays open latest on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commons lists regular-semester Friday hours of 7:30 a.m.–12 a.m. and Saturday hours of 8 a.m.–12 a.m.
cards.source_title: The Commons – UMBC
cards.access_notes: Regular-semester building hours list midnight closing Friday and Saturday; posted semester and holiday schedules differ.

cards.title: McDonald's on Frederick Road
cards.subtitle: 501 Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
cards.notes: For a later pickup, use the drive-thru; the restaurant page lists it as open 24 hours while the lobby closes at midnight.
cards.short_summary: A Frederick Road drive-thru listed around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald's lists this location’s drive-thru as open 24 hours daily and its lobby as open until midnight.
cards.source_title: McDonald's – 501 Frederick Road
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed 24 hours daily; lobby hours are 6 a.m.–12 a.m. daily.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Baltimore National Pike
cards.subtitle: 6200 Baltimore National Pike, Catonsville, MD
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru for the latest listed access; the location page gives a 4 a.m. daily drive-thru close and a 10 p.m. dining-room close.
cards.short_summary: A Catonsville drive-thru listed until 4 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists this location’s drive-thru hours as 7 a.m.–4 a.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell – 6200 Baltimore National Pike
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed until 4 a.m. daily; dine-in is listed until 10 p.m., so use the appropriate service.

cards.title: Hip Hop Fish & Chicken
cards.subtitle: 6400 Baltimore National Pike, Catonsville, MD
cards.notes: Check Toast before placing an order; its restaurant page lists daily late service, extending to 3 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Baltimore National Pike counter with late listed ordering.
cards.evidence_claim: The restaurant’s Toast page lists hours until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Hip Hop Fish & Chicken Catonsville – Toast
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 10:15 a.m.–2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 10:15 a.m.–3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Kiani's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 5808 Johnny Cake Road, Catonsville, MD
cards.notes: Use Kiani's ordering page to check the day’s closing time; it lists midnight on Friday and Saturday and 10:30 p.m. Sunday through Thursday.
cards.short_summary: A Johnny Cake Road pizza shop with midnight weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Kiani's lists Friday and Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–12 a.m. and Sunday–Thursday hours until 10:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: Kiani's Pizza
cards.access_notes: Weekend service is listed until midnight; Sunday–Thursday service is listed until 10:30 p.m.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on Frederick Road
cards.subtitle: 6415 Frederick Road, Catonsville, MD
cards.notes: Place a carryout or delivery order before the published weekend close; this location lists midnight hours on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Frederick Road pizza option with midnight weekend service.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut lists Friday and Saturday restaurant hours of 10:30 a.m.–12 a.m. at 6415 Frederick Road.
cards.source_title: Pizza Hut – 6415 Frederick Road
cards.access_notes: Carryout and delivery are listed until midnight Friday and Saturday; other days close at 11 p.m.

cards.title: Jennings Cafe
cards.subtitle: 808–810 Frederick Road, Catonsville, MD
cards.notes: For a sit-down meal, aim for Friday or Saturday; Jennings lists its kitchen open until 11 p.m. on both nights.
cards.short_summary: A Catonsville restaurant with an 11 p.m. weekend kitchen close.
cards.evidence_claim: Jennings Cafe lists Friday–Saturday kitchen hours of 11 a.m.–11 p.m.
cards.source_title: Jennings Cafe
cards.access_notes: Kitchen service is listed until 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday; the restaurant’s bar hours are not relevant to this card.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten distinct UMBC places for studying, making, gathering, movement, and campus culture, supported by direct university sources.

cards.title: The Commons
cards.subtitle: UMBC student union, central campus
cards.notes: Use the student union as a practical between-class meeting point: its listed spaces include lounges, student organization areas, dining, and a game room.
cards.short_summary: A central building for meetings, services, meals, and campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC describes The Commons as its student union and says it hosts social, cultural, and recreational activities before, between, and after classes.
cards.source_title: The Commons – UMBC
cards.access_notes: Check the Commons site for current building and department hours.

cards.title: The Commons Terrace
cards.subtitle: Outdoor terrace at The Commons
cards.notes: Bring a conversation or a packed meal outdoors when conditions allow; UMBC identifies the terrace as a lunch meeting spot and event venue.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Commons gathering area used for meals and programmed events.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says the Commons Terrace is a regular meeting spot for lunch and hosts concerts, ice cream socials, and campus festivals.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Destinations – UMBC
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent; consult event listings for programmed activities.

cards.title: The Quad
cards.subtitle: Lawn outside The Commons
cards.notes: Use the open lawn as a simple rendezvous point before a Commons event, or pause there on a walk between the library and student-union spaces.
cards.short_summary: A central campus green immediately associated with The Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s welcome guide lists The Quad among the outdoor resources at The Commons, and its destinations page identifies Quadmania as an all-campus spring festival.
cards.source_title: UMBC Welcome Guide
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor space; follow posted event setups and campus policies.

cards.title: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.subtitle: 1000 Hilltop Circle
cards.notes: Start here when your group needs a shared academic base: the building combines broad collections with designated study areas and library services.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s main library building and a prominent campus study destination.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC calls the Albin O. Kuhn Library the visual centerpiece of campus and identifies it as open to the general public.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Destinations – UMBC
cards.access_notes: Building access and borrowing privileges differ; check the library’s current hours and visitor guidance.

cards.title: Albin O. Kuhn Library Gallery
cards.subtitle: First floor, Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Pair a library stop with the current exhibition: look for interpretive displays from UMBC collections and check gallery information before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor exhibition space within UMBC’s library building.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC states that Library Gallery exhibitions showcase photography, rare books, and other materials from the library’s collections.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Destinations – UMBC
cards.access_notes: Gallery is listed in Library room 105; verify current exhibition and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Retriever Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Choose this library space for a collaborative session: arrange the mobile furniture, use whiteboards or monitors, and leave quiet-floor work for later.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour collaborative library environment with flexible furnishings.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC Library describes the Retriever Learning Center as a 24-hour space for group study, discussion, collaboration, and academic coaching.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms – UMBC Library
cards.access_notes: The library lists the RLC as 24 hours; access may require UMBC credentials or vary during closures.

cards.title: Digital Media Lab
cards.subtitle: Room 216H, Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Reserve recording space or use the editing workstations when a class project needs audio, video, or graphic-design production rather than a standard desk.
cards.short_summary: A library media-creation lab with editing tools and recording spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Media Lab provides UMBC students, faculty, and staff with tools to create and edit audio, video, and graphic-design objects.
cards.source_title: Digital Media Lab – UMBC Library
cards.access_notes: Available to UMBC community members; book recording rooms and review current equipment and hours information.

cards.entity_name: Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture
cards.title: Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Building, 105
cards.notes: Check whether an exhibition is on view, then make this a focused art stop with a friend or a change of scene from library study.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s Fine Arts Building exhibition and public-programming venue.
cards.evidence_claim: CADVC lists its location in the Fine Arts Building and states that its public hours apply when exhibitions are on view and the university is open.
cards.source_title: Visit Us – Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture
cards.access_notes: Currently exhibition-dependent; confirm the gallery’s status and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Retriever Activities Center
cards.subtitle: 1000 Hilltop Circle
cards.notes: Meet up for a walk on the indoor track, a scheduled class, or a workout; check facility rules and the current recreation schedule first.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s recreation facility for fitness, aquatics, courts, and an indoor track.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC lists the RAC’s fitness studio, weight room, cardio balcony, arena track, and aquatics center among its facilities.
cards.source_title: Athletics – UMBC Welcome Guide
cards.access_notes: Current RAC hours are Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–8 p.m. and weekends noon–6 p.m.; hours and eligibility may change.

cards.title: Conservation and Environmental Research Areas
cards.subtitle: CERA trails near UMBC’s Research Park
cards.notes: Take the marked interpretive route from the Herbert Run Greenway entrance, stay on established paths, and use the CERA map to orient your walk.
cards.short_summary: A mapped campus-adjacent wooded research and trail area.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC provides directions to CERA and identifies the Herbert Run Greenway and CERA Interpretive Trail by their marked blazes.
cards.source_title: Visit CERA – UMBC Department of Geography & Environmental Systems
cards.access_notes: Use the department’s route and trail map; remain on marked paths and plan for daylight and weather.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing

cards.title: Set up a casual court game
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Bring a few friends and check the RAC schedule before using the multipurpose courts for a casual basketball, volleyball, badminton, or soccer session.
cards.short_summary: A flexible indoor court option for an informal group game.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC identifies the RAC Courts as multipurpose courts for open recreation and says students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; verify court availability around classes, practices, and events.

cards.title: Walk laps on the arena track
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Meet a walking partner at the indoor arena track, then use open-recreation time for an easy conversation-paced lap session.
cards.short_summary: An indoor walking hang that does not depend on the weather.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC states that the RAC Arena Track is used for open recreation and that students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; confirm open-recreation availability before heading over.

cards.entity_name: Indoor Aquatics Facility Open Recreation Swim
cards.title: Plan an open-recreation swim
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Coordinate with friends for an indoor pool visit and follow posted recreation-swim rules, including required pool-deck footwear noted by UMBC.
cards.short_summary: A year-round indoor swim option when recreation-swim time is available.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says its indoor aquatics facility is used for open recreation swim and that students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; check the aquatics schedule and recreation-swim requirements first.

cards.title: Do a side-by-side cardio session
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Pick adjacent machines in the RAC Cardio Zone and set a comfortable shared workout length; treadmills, bikes, rowers, and ellipticals are listed.
cards.short_summary: A low-planning workout hang with several machine choices.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC lists cardio equipment in the RAC Cardio Zone and states that students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; use equipment according to RAC rules and availability.

cards.title: Catch up while using the cardio balcony
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Use the main-level cardio balcony during open recreation for a paired workout overlooking the RAC gymnasium floor.
cards.short_summary: A social cardio option with a view into the gymnasium.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says the RAC Cardio Balcony is used for open recreation and that students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; check for schedule changes or class use.

cards.title: Train together in Weight Room 060
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Pair up for a strength session in the RAC’s free-weight-focused room, choosing movements and loads appropriate to each participant’s experience.
cards.short_summary: An open-recreation weight-room session for strength-training partners.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says Weight Room 060 is used for open recreation and that students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; follow RAC equipment rules and yield to scheduled use.

cards.title: Try a machine-based workout together
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Use the RAC’s machine-oriented Weight Room 063 for a shared endurance-focused or beginner-friendly strength routine during open recreation.
cards.short_summary: A machine-based option for a paced, shared workout.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says Weight Room 063 is used for open recreation and that students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; check equipment availability and posted room guidance.

cards.title: Build a short circuit in the fitness room
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Choose a few functional-fitness stations with friends—such as kettlebells, medicine balls, ropes, or sleds—and leave time to reset equipment.
cards.short_summary: A varied equipment space for a self-guided small-group circuit.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC lists the Functional Fitness Room’s exercise equipment and states that students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; select activities suitable for the space and follow posted rules.

cards.title: Use the multipurpose room for open recreation
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center
cards.notes: Check whether the first-floor multipurpose room is open, then use the shared indoor space for an easy, low-equipment group activity.
cards.short_summary: A reservable-feeling indoor option when it is in open-recreation use.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC states that the first-floor RAC Multi-Purpose Room is available for open recreation and that students, faculty, and staff may use recreation facilities free with a valid Black & Gold ID.
cards.source_title: Facilities – Recreation and Physical Education – UMBC
cards.access_notes: For current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; availability varies because the room also hosts classes and events.

cards.title: Look through a CADVC exhibition
cards.subtitle: Center for Art, Design, and Visual Culture, Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Visit the CADVC gallery with a friend and give yourselves time to compare observations; check its visitor information for the current exhibition and gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: A free public gallery visit in UMBC’s Fine Arts Building.
cards.evidence_claim: CADVC states that its exhibitions and events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: absolute alternatives, the 2026 Arts+ UMBC Faculty Exhibition – CADVC
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; consult CADVC visitor information for current exhibition dates, hours, directions, and parking details.

warnings: RAC access is free for current UMBC students, faculty, and staff with a valid Black & Gold ID; it is not represented here as public access.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, university-documented study environments in UMBC’s Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery, spanning quiet work, group collaboration, media creation, and presentation practice.

cards.title: Reservable Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Reserve up to five days ahead for a group session; bring your work plan and use the room’s whiteboards and computers to keep everyone aligned.
cards.short_summary: A bookable group-work option with whiteboards and computers.
cards.evidence_claim: The library lists 14 group study rooms for UMBC students, faculty, and staff; they may be reserved up to five days ahead for up to three hours per person or group daily.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: Available to UMBC faculty, students, and staff. Reserve up to five days ahead; three-hour daily limit per person or group.

cards.title: Reservable Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Book a focused solo block up to five days ahead, then use the quiet room to separate concentrated reading or writing from busier library areas.
cards.short_summary: Bookable quiet rooms designed for individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: The library lists eight reservable individual study rooms for UMBC faculty, students, and staff, with reservations up to five days ahead and a three-hour daily limit per person.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: Available to UMBC faculty, students, and staff. Quiet rooms; reserve up to five days ahead for up to three hours daily.

cards.title: Open Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Use the listed room numbers to find an open room when your schedule changes; these first-come spaces suit an impromptu individual work session.
cards.short_summary: Eighteen first-come rooms for unplanned study time.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies 18 open study rooms that students may use on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served for students; consult the library’s listed room numbers.

cards.title: Presentation Practice Room (257)
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery, Room 257
cards.notes: Bring a flash drive and rehearse your talk with the one-button recording system, then review the recording before class, an interview, or a group presentation.
cards.short_summary: A rehearsal room that records presentations for review.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 257 is set up for students to practice presentations and speeches using a one-button recording system; reservations take precedence over walk-up use and the key is available at the Check Out Desk.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: Reservations are not required but take precedence over walk-up appointments. Check out the key at the library’s Check Out Desk.

cards.title: Simmons Collaboration Room (368)
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery, Room 368
cards.notes: Reserve this small-group room when a shared screen will help; Chromecast can stream from a laptop, tablet, or phone to the room’s smart TV.
cards.short_summary: A small-group room with a conference table and Chromecast-enabled TV.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons Collaboration Room 368 is available to UMBC students, faculty, and staff, with a conference table and smart TV with Chromecast; groups of three to seven may reserve it for up to three hours.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: Available to UMBC students, faculty, and staff. Reserve for groups of 3–7 for periods up to three hours.

cards.title: Richard Roberts Seminar Room (140)
cards.subtitle: Retriever Learning Center, Room 140
cards.notes: Plan a team session around the projector and large monitor, and reserve a two-hour block when you need a whiteboard-ready room for shared materials.
cards.short_summary: A reservable RLC seminar room with display and projection tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The Richard Roberts Seminar Room in the RLC has a conference table, large-screen monitor, projector, laptop cables, and whiteboards; UMBC students, faculty, and staff may reserve it for group periods up to two hours.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: Available to UMBC students, faculty, and staff; group reservations are limited to two hours.

cards.title: Digital Media Lab
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Use an editing workstation for media coursework, or book the Whisper Room or Audio/Video Recording Room when a project needs controlled recording space.
cards.short_summary: A media-production workspace with recording rooms and editing software.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Media Lab is open to UMBC students, faculty, and staff and includes computer workspaces with editing software, a Whisper Room, and an Audio/Video Recording Room.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open to UMBC students, faculty, and staff. Book time for the Whisper Room or Audio/Video Recording Room.

cards.title: Retriever Learning Center (RLC)
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Arrange the mobile furniture around your group’s task, then use the movable whiteboards and large monitors to work through problems, drafts, or slides together.
cards.short_summary: A flexible collaboration space with mobile furniture, whiteboards, and monitors.
cards.evidence_claim: The RLC provides mobile furniture, movable whiteboards, large monitors, computers, and individual and group study space; the library designates it as a 24-hour space.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: The library lists the RLC as a 24-hour space; check the library’s current hours page for exceptions.

cards.title: AOK Library Floors 3 and 4
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Choose these whisper-level floors when reading or drafting needs fewer interruptions; library PCs are available if you need to switch from laptop work.
cards.short_summary: Quiet library floors with computers for individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: The library designates its third and fourth floors as quiet areas where users should keep volume to a whisper, and reports 22 student-use PCs on these floors.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: Quiet areas: keep volume to a whisper. Access follows current library building hours.

cards.title: AOK Library Floors 5 and 6
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Head here for tasks that benefit from silence, such as close reading or exam preparation; use one of the available PCs if a campus workstation is needed.
cards.short_summary: Absolute-quiet library floors with student-use computers.
cards.evidence_claim: The library designates its fifth and sixth floors as absolute quiet areas at all times and reports 32 student-use PCs on those floors.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms | Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.access_notes: Absolute quiet at all times. Access follows current library building hours.

cards.title: Plan a meal at East Drive Kitchen

cards.title: Eat on the East Drive corridor

cards.evidence_claim: UMBC lists Cactus Silvestre Tex-Mex Restaurant at 5406 East Drive in Arbutus and identifies the nearby Arbutus Line stop.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UMBC rituals and recurring community events, from a golden-nosed mascot to a class-free midday block.

cards.title: The scheduled Free Hour
cards.subtitle: UMBC academic calendar, Monday–Wednesday–Friday
cards.notes: Plan a club meeting, campus event, or lunch during the noon-to-1 p.m. class-free block on Monday, Wednesday, or Friday.
cards.short_summary: A student-created class-free hour that remains part of UMBC life.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s SGA history says students called for a Monday, Wednesday, and Friday Free Hour with no scheduled classes in 1970, and that it continues to exist.
cards.source_title: History – Student Government Association – UMBC
cards.access_notes: The university’s event-services guidance identifies Free Hour as noon–1 p.m. on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

cards.title: Rub the Retriever’s golden nose
cards.subtitle: True Grit statue near the Administration Building and RAC
cards.notes: Find the bronze True Grit statue and add a quick nose rub before finals, Convocation, or Commencement for the campus good-luck ritual.
cards.short_summary: Students mark milestones and seek finals luck at the mascot sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC documents that students and alumni rub the bronze True Grit sculpture’s nose for good luck, including around Convocation, Commencement, and finals.
cards.source_title: How To Be A Retriever! – UMBC
cards.access_notes: The source locates the sculpture on the plaza between the Administration Building and Retriever Athletic Center.

cards.title: Come home in black and gold
cards.subtitle: Annual UMBC Homecoming week
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming calendar for the annual week of reunions, carnival activities, athletics, and Retriever-pride events.
cards.short_summary: A multi-day gathering that has connected the UMBC community since 1976.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says Homecoming has been an annual multi-day event since 1976; its current site describes annual bonfire, reunions, carnival, and athletic events.
cards.source_title: Homecoming – UMBC
cards.access_notes: The Homecoming site lists the 2026 celebration for the week of October 31; consult its schedule as events are announced.

cards.title: Start Homecoming around the bonfire
cards.subtitle: Erickson Field
cards.notes: Join the Homecoming kickoff on Erickson Field and follow organizer instructions around the professionally managed annual bonfire.
cards.short_summary: A student-originated fire-lighting tradition that has anchored Homecoming since 2004.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC reports that the first Homecoming Bonfire was held in 2004 and that the tradition has continued annually as a Homecoming centerpiece.
cards.source_title: Building the bonfire from scratch – UMBC
cards.access_notes: UMBC’s traditions page identifies Erickson Field as the bonfire location; attend only during the scheduled, staffed event.

cards.title: Close spring with Quadmania
cards.subtitle: Annual spring festival hosted by UMBC’s Student Events Board
cards.notes: Watch for the spring schedule and choose from the outdoor festival, games, music, and Retriever Quest activities offered that year.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s end-of-academic-year spring festival.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s Student Events Board identifies Quadmania as its annual spring festival and describes music, an all-day carnival, and Retriever Quest.
cards.source_title: Annual Events – Student Events Board – UMBC
cards.access_notes: Programming changes by year; use the Student Events Board’s current announcements for date and participation details.

cards.title: See Pangea’s cultural showcase
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week cultural student-organization event
cards.notes: During Welcome Week, look for the student-led showcase to watch performances and meet cultural organizations sharing their work.
cards.short_summary: A Welcome Week cultural showcase created by UMBC students.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says Pangea debuted in fall 2016 after students worked with cultural organizations and staff, and that it became a campus tradition.
cards.source_title: SPACES: Co-Creating Communities at UMBC – UMBC
cards.access_notes: UMBC lists Pangea as a Welcome Week cultural showcase; confirm the current program and location before attending.

cards.title: Sing “Our UMBC” at milestones
cards.subtitle: Convocation and Commencement ceremony tradition
cards.notes: Listen for the alma mater at Convocation or Commencement, and join the singing if you know the words and ceremony guidance permits.
cards.short_summary: A 2006 alma mater sung at UMBC’s major academic ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC states that its alma mater debuted in 2006 and is sung at Convocation and Commencement.
cards.source_title: How To Be A Retriever! – UMBC
cards.access_notes: This is part of scheduled university ceremonies; ceremony access and participation guidance can vary.

cards.title: Take a finals break at Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: End-of-semester event at True Grit’s dining hall
cards.notes: During finals season, check Residential Student Association announcements for the late-evening breakfast and stress-break programming at True Grit’s.
cards.short_summary: An end-of-semester gathering that turns the dining hall into a finals break.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC describes Midnight Breakfast as a Residential Student Association tradition held before finals, with breakfast and community activities at True Grit’s.
cards.source_title: How To Be A Retriever! – UMBC
cards.access_notes: The cited UMBC account says the event usually runs 10 p.m.–2 a.m.; confirm the current semester’s time and entry requirements.

cards.title: Make election night a campus event
cards.subtitle: The Commons, during U.S. presidential election cycles
cards.notes: During a presidential-election year, look for campus partners’ program details for the watch party, discussions, games, and civic-engagement activities.
cards.short_summary: A UMBC election-night gathering built around civic engagement and community.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says its Election Night Extravaganza has created a community space around presidential elections since 2004, with the Center for Democracy and Civic Life and student governments hosting.
cards.source_title: How To Be A Retriever! – UMBC
cards.access_notes: This tradition is tied to U.S. presidential election cycles; follow current UMBC civic-life announcements for details.

cards.title: Cheer the Homecoming Puppy Parade
cards.subtitle: Erickson Field during UMBC Homecoming
cards.notes: At Homecoming, watch costumed dogs and their people parade on Erickson Field; bring a pet only if the current event rules allow it.
cards.short_summary: A dog-centered Homecoming tradition that became annual after returning in 2019.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says the Puppy Parade began for its 2016 fiftieth birthday and became an annual Homecoming tradition after returning in 2019.
cards.source_title: Celebrate Your Retriever Spirit At Homecoming 2023 – UMBC
cards.access_notes: The cited UMBC coverage places the parade on Erickson Field; consult the current Homecoming schedule and pet-participation rules.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Maryland-Baltimore County, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented to UMBC’s campus spaces, food options, recreation, and recurring student activities.

cards.title: Start at the Campus Information Center
cards.subtitle: The Commons • first stop for campus questions
cards.notes: Begin here to get oriented and ask for practical campus information before choosing the rest of your weekend stops.
cards.short_summary: A central help desk inside UMBC’s student union.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC identifies the Campus Information Center in The Commons as the first place to go with a question.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Destinations
cards.access_notes: Located in The Commons; check the Commons site for service hours before visiting.

cards.title: Get the Lay of the Land at The Commons
cards.subtitle: UMBC’s student union
cards.notes: Walk through the student union, note the event and service spaces, and pick a comfortable meeting point for later.
cards.short_summary: The campus hub for student services, gathering, dining, and recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC describes The Commons as its student union and a hub for social, cultural, and recreational activities.
cards.source_title: The Commons
cards.access_notes: Building hours vary by semester and may change; consult the Commons page before going.

cards.title: Plan a Meal at True Grit's
cards.subtitle: Dining hall in the residential area
cards.notes: If you have a dining plan, use this stop to learn the dining-hall routine and check the current menu or service period.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s all-you-care-to-eat dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC states that True Grit’s is its all-you-care-to-eat dining hall, offering breakfast, lunch, dinner, and late-night meals.
cards.source_title: Where to Eat
cards.access_notes: Meal access and dining hours depend on the current schedule and meal plan; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Take a Break in the Gameroom
cards.subtitle: Second floor of The Commons
cards.notes: After lunch, locate the Gameroom and see whether its billiards, board games, or television areas fit your group’s pace.
cards.short_summary: A Commons recreation space with games and shared seating.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s welcome guide lists the Gameroom in The Commons, and its Commons information describes billiards tables, board games, and TVs there.
cards.source_title: The Commons | UMBC Welcome Guide
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of The Commons; game availability and any checkout rules may vary.

cards.entity_name: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery Atrium
cards.title: Settle into the AOK Library Atrium
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Use the atrium as a casual regrouping point, then decide whether your group wants quiet work, conversation, or another campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A social study area at UMBC’s library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s library describes the atrium as a social and conversation space that is open 24 hours a day.
cards.source_title: AOK Study Spaces and Lockers
cards.access_notes: The atrium is listed as open 24 hours; access procedures can differ from the library building’s posted hours.

cards.title: Look for an Exhibit at AOK Library Gallery
cards.subtitle: Inside Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Check the current display on arrival and give yourselves time to view it rather than treating the gallery as a pass-through.
cards.short_summary: An exhibition space within UMBC’s library building.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s international-student resource page states that the AOK Library’s gallery and atrium display exhibits throughout the year.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources | Office of International Students and Scholars
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions change; consult the library’s current information for display and building access details.

cards.entity_name: Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture
cards.title: Visit the Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Make this an afternoon art stop: confirm the current exhibition or public program, then allow time to look through the galleries.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s art, design, and visual-culture exhibition venue.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC identifies the Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture in the Fine Arts Building as a forum for research, exhibition, publication, and public programming.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Destinations
cards.access_notes: Located in the Fine Arts Building; confirm current gallery and program access before traveling over.

cards.title: Move Around at the RAC
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center (RAC)
cards.notes: Bring your campus credentials, check the day’s facility rules, and choose a realistic workout, swim, court, or track activity.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s recreation and physical-activity center.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC lists RAC amenities including a fitness studio, weight room, cardio balcony, arena track, and aquatics center.
cards.source_title: Athletics | UMBC Welcome Guide
cards.access_notes: RAC hours are subject to change; its current hours page lists weekend building hours of noon–6 p.m.

cards.title: Check the Intramural Sports Options
cards.subtitle: UMBC Recreation activity
cards.notes: Look over the current intramural schedule and registration details, then choose an activity that fits your experience and availability.
cards.short_summary: Organized team, individual, and special-event recreation for the UMBC community.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC states that intramural sports offer team, individual, and special events throughout the academic year, with full-time students eligible to participate.
cards.source_title: Athletics | UMBC Welcome Guide
cards.access_notes: Eligibility, sports offered, registration, and fees can vary by activity; check UMBC Recreation before joining.

cards.title: Save Involvement Fest for Your Next Campus Visit
cards.subtitle: Retriever Activities Center (RAC)
cards.notes: When the next fest is announced, use the organization list and floor map to make a short, intentional route through clubs of interest.
cards.short_summary: A UMBC student-organization fair held in the RAC.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s Involvement Fest information identifies the event as taking place in the Retriever Activities Center and provides a full list of student organizations and event maps.
cards.source_title: Involvement Fest Event Information
cards.access_notes: This is a scheduled recurring welcome activity, not a guaranteed every-weekend event; check UMBC’s current welcome programming.
